items.title: Don Alias interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 6, 2002
items.q: And they would come through and they would see Chuck and he’s still surviving off of that stuff.

ctx.x: “Land of Make Believe.” He’s still surviving in that market, where people will come, they’re older, forties and fifties, but still remember that scene, you know, because the seventies was a great time. And they would come through and they would see Chuck and he’s still surviving off of that stuff. But surviving really good. Because he gets good musicians, and we get a chance to play.
I saw Mick Jagger listed amongst — wait a minute, who haven’t you played with? Louis Armstrong I guess.
